Within a broad 2-digit sector, firms with similar EBITDA and gross margins turn a dollar of sales into similar cash flow, so they should be valued at similar sales multiples. Growth is added as a secondary driver, and the median guards against extreme peers.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.570, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.4 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Finest-industry median cascade
proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 4-digit SIC code share products, customers, cost structures and risk, so their multiples cluster most tightly. A plain median over the finest industry with enough members, stepping back to 3-digit and then 2-digit codes, is fully transparent. It also avoids the narrow growth band that removed good peers and added noise.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error between 0.315 and 0.335, beating the L3/L2 industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | k=all, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2] -> []

proposals.name: Sector plus margin-band EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: A firm's sales multiple is mostly its profitability capitalised, so peers should first be held to a narrow EBITDA-margin band (plus or minus 5 points) inside the same 2-digit sector, then ranked by margin and growth. This replaces the leverage-based ranking, which affects how EV is split between debt and equity more than how large EV is. If the sector-plus-band pool is too thin, the rule falls back to margin-matched firms from any sector before falling back to the sector alone.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.560, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [same industry_l2]

proposals.name: Cross-industry fundamental twins for EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: This is a calculated risk. For EV/Sales, a firm's margin structure and growth may predict its multiple better than its SIC code, since SIC codes group firms with very different economics. Matching on EBITDA margin, gross margin, growth and R&D intensity across all non-financial firms, and taking the median of 20 such twins, tests whether fundamentals alone beat industry labels.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.590, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years; if it fails, industry membership carries information that margins do not.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.5, rnd_intensity 0.3 | k=20, median, min_peers=5

proposals.name: Sector growth-margin-leverage neighbours (EBITDA)
proposals.mechanism: This puts the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple drivers into the peer choice. Within a 2-digit sector, peers similar in growth, EBITDA margin and net leverage should share the target's EBITDA multiple: growth and margin reflect future cash flow, and leverage reflects risk. A wider k of 20 and a median keep the estimate stable, in place of the size- and capex-based harmonic mean.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.330, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=20, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Growth-and-reinvestment peers within L3, median
proposals.mechanism: My view is that within an industry, EV/EBITDA mostly differs because of growth and how much of EBITDA gets eaten by capex. Firms that grow alike and reinvest alike should trade at similar EBITDA multiples. Recipe 1 had the right idea but lost to the baseline because L2 is too coarse and the harmonic mean gets pulled down by low-multiple outliers, so I'd tighten to L3 and switch to the median, which is the natural aggregator for a log-error metric.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.333 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with coverage of at least 99%.

proposals.name: Margin-matched EV/Sales peers within L3
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales is just EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so margin is the main thing a sales multiple has to get right. I think this is the single most promising direction for EV/Sales. Recipe 2 ranked on ROIC and assets, which only proxy for margin, and averaged with a mean that right-skewed sales multiples inflate. Ranking directly on EBITDA margin with a little growth, and taking the median, should fix both problems.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.56 (clearly below the 0.603 baseline) and beats the industry median in all 4 years.

proposals.name: Finest-industry median with cascading fallback
proposals.mechanism: This one is a control on how narrow the industry definition should be: 4-digit SIC peers share product markets, customers and cost structures more closely than 3-digit peers, so their multiples should cluster tighter. Recipe 3's ±0.1 growth band threw away good peers on a noisy one-year number and the mean amplified outliers. I'd drop the band and just test whether L4 with a median, falling back to L3 and then L2, beats L3.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.333 in at least 3 of 4 years; if it is not below 0.333 overall, industry granularity beyond L3 is not where the gains are.

proposals.name: Profitability-profile EV/Sales peers within L2
proposals.mechanism: Recipe 4 came closest to the baseline, but leverage doesn't really drive an enterprise-value multiple. What should drive it is how much of each sales dollar turns into operating profit, plus how fast sales grow. Matching on EBITDA margin and gross margin (pricing power) and growth within the broader L2 group gives a bigger pool to find close matches in, and the ranking does the job the narrow industry filter used to do.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.58 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
proposals.compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []

proposals.name: Hard margin band for EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: I'd test a harder version of the margin idea: only allow peers whose EBITDA margin is within 5 points of the target's, so a 5%-margin distributor never gets valued off a 30%-margin brand owner in the same 2-digit SIC. Recipe 5 failed because L4 with k=19 just took nearly every L4 firm and averaged them with a skewed mean, so ranking had no effect. Here the margin band does the main work and size and growth break ties.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.57 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years; it should beat recipe 2 if margin matters non-linearly.

proposals.name: Value-driver peers (ROIC and growth) within L3
proposals.mechanism: In a standard value-driver model, the EBITDA multiple depends on growth and on the return earned on reinvested capital. Two firms growing at the same rate deserve the same multiple only if they need similar reinvestment to get there, and ROIC captures that. Recipe 6 matched on size and capex, which is only half of this, and used the harmonic mean. I'd rank on ROIC and growth with light size matching and take the median of 12 peers to keep it stable.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.333 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so firms in the same industry that convert sales into profit at similar rates should trade at similar sales multiples. Matching on EBITDA and gross margin inside L3 and using the median of 8 nearest peers targets the main driver of the sales multiple while staying robust to outliers.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.603 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.name: L3 growth-and-leverage neighbours, median
proposals.mechanism: Within an industry, faster-growing firms carry higher EV/EBITDA, and net leverage proxies for risk and for how mature and cash-generative the business is. Ranking L3 peers on growth plus net debt to EBITDA, without the narrow hard growth band that discarded useful peers, and taking a median of 20 peers should keep peer sets large and relevant.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.333 and beats the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.

proposals.name: L2 profitability-growth-R&D neighbours, median
proposals.mechanism: A firm's sales multiple reflects its profit margin, its growth, and its investment in intangibles (R&D is expensed, which lowers current margins but supports future cash flows). Ranking within a 2-digit industry on these three drivers gives a wider pool in which genuinely similar economics can be found, and the median of 12 limits the effect of extreme multiples.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.603 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.name: L3 EBITDA-margin band, median
proposals.mechanism: Because EV/Sales scales almost mechanically with the EBITDA margin, a hard screen that keeps only same-industry firms within 7 percentage points of the target's margin removes the largest source of error in a plain industry median. Using all surviving peers with a median keeps the rule simple, with fallbacks to a wider industry and then to plain industry peers.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error below 0.603 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

proposals.name: L2 cash-conversion neighbours, median
proposals.mechanism: EV/EBITDA is higher when less EBITDA is used up by capex and when R&D spending points to growth options, while margin level shows competitive position. Ranking within 2-digit industries on capex intensity, R&D intensity, EBITDA margin and size picks peers with similar cash conversion and risk, and a median of 12 avoids the downward bias of the harmonic mean.
proposals.prediction: Exploration median error at or below 0.333 and beats the industry median in at least 2 of 4 years.

proposals.name: L3 growth-and-return neighbors, median
proposals.mechanism: In a DCF the EV/EBITDA multiple is driven mostly by expected growth and by the return on reinvested capital, so peers in the same 3-digit industry that match on recent sales growth and ROIC should share the target's warranted multiple. A larger k with median aggregation (instead of harmonic mean over 10 L2 peers) limits the influence of outlier peers while keeping the economic matching.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.333 (the L3 industry-median baseline), beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.

proposals.name: L3 margin-matched EV/Sales, median
proposals.mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so within an industry the main reason sales multiples differ is profitability. Ranking same-industry peers mainly on EBITDA margin, with a small weight on growth, removes most of the cross-firm spread in sales multiples, and the median guards against extreme peers.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.603, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.

proposals.name: Finest-industry median with nested fallback
proposals.mechanism: Firms in the same 4-digit SIC code share products, customers, cost structures and risk, so their EBITDA multiples should cluster more tightly than at the 3-digit level. Removing the narrow growth band and the noisy rank features, and stepping back to L3 and then L2 only when the L4 group is thin, keeps the closest business matches and still covers every firm.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.333, beating the L3 industry median in at least 2 of 4 exploration years.

proposals.name: L2 margin-band EV/Sales
proposals.mechanism: Within a broad industry, firms that earn a similar EBITDA margin turn each dollar of sales into similar cash flow, so they should trade at similar sales multiples. A hard margin band inside the 2-digit industry, ranked on margin with a light size weight, targets the profitability gap directly; fallbacks keep coverage when the band is thin.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.595 (previous Recipe 4) and below 0.603, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.

proposals.name: L2 profitability-growth-R&D neighbors, median
proposals.mechanism: Sales multiples reflect margin, growth and intangible investment: R&D-heavy firms expense spending that builds future value, which raises EV/Sales relative to current profits. Matching on EBITDA margin, growth and R&D intensity inside the 2-digit industry (not the thin 4-digit group) gives enough peers with similar value drivers, and the median replaces the outlier-sensitive mean.
proposals.prediction: Median error below 0.603, beating the industry median in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.

proposals.name: L3 size-and-growth neighbors, wide k median
proposals.mechanism: Larger, faster-growing firms within an industry tend to have lower risk or higher expected cash-flow growth, both of which raise EV/EBITDA. Replacing capex intensity with growth, widening k to 20 and using the median keeps the industry anchor while adding a light adjustment for the two most important valuation differences inside an industry.
proposals.prediction: Median error at or below 0.333, beating the industry median in at least 2 of 4 exploration years.
